query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended as energetic structural materials, what single testable hypothesis identifies an intervention that could improve ductility and uniform deformability without sacrificing high strength or impact-induced energy release? State the proposed intervention, its hypothesized mechanism, the improvement expected relative to the untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing 8–12 at.% Al and 4–8 at.% Ti into a baseline Nb–Mo–Ta–W refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) followed by an 800 °C/10 h aging treatment that nucleates ~15 vol % nanoscale B2-ordered (Al,Ti)(Nb,Ta) precipitates within the BCC matrix will raise room-temperature uniform elongation from ≤2 % to ≥8 % while retaining ≥90 % of the baseline 0.2 % proof strength (≥1.2 GPa) and maintaining the same (±10 %) specific impact-induced exothermic energy release.
generation.material_initial_state: Homogenized single-phase BCC Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 (at.%) high-entropy alloy with average grain size ≈30 µm, exhibiting ~1.3 GPa yield strength and <2 % uniform elongation at 25 °C.
generation.intervention: Add 8–12 at.% Al and 4–8 at.% Ti (substituting equiatomically for Nb, Mo, Ta, W), arc-melt, homogenize (1200 °C/24 h), then age at 800 °C for 10 h to precipitate ~15 vol % coherent B2 nanoscale precipitates.
generation.conditions: Quasi-static tensile testing at 25 °C and 10-3 s-1 strain rate; Taylor impact or light-gas-gun impact in air at ~1 km s-1 to trigger energetic reaction.
generation.structural_mediator: A dual-phase microstructure of coherent 10–50 nm B2 (Al,Ti)(Nb,Ta) precipitates uniformly dispersed in a BCC refractory matrix, producing transformation-/twinning-assisted plasticity and precipitation strengthening.
generation.mechanism:
1. The softer, ordered B2 precipitates promote strain partitioning and reversible diffuse shearing (TRIP/TWIP-like) that delay necking, increasing uniform deformability.
2. Coherent B2/BCC interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion, sustaining high work-hardening and retaining high yield strength.
3. Al and Ti maintain or enhance exothermic oxidation during high-velocity impact, so total chemical energy release is not reduced.
generation.predicted_outcome:
Compared with the untreated baseline alloy, the modified alloy will exhibit:
• Uniform elongation ≥8 % (≥4× increase).
• 0.2 % proof strength ≥1.1× baseline (≥1.4 GPa expected) with ultimate strength ≥1.6 GPa.
• Specific energy release on impact (kJ g-1) within ±10 % of baseline value.
generation.baseline: Arc-melted, homogenized Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 RHEA with single BCC phase, ~1.3 GPa yield strength, <2 % uniform elongation, and established impact-induced heat of reaction H0.
generation.boundary: Effect is expected for total (Al+Ti) additions of 10–20 at.% and aging temperatures 700–900 °C that give 10–20 vol % B2 precipitates. Outside this range (e.g., >25 vol % B2 or no aging), strength may fall or brittleness may return. Benefit is specific to room-temperature and moderate strain rates; at >600 °C the B2 phase coarsens and ductility gains may vanish.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of elongation increase and precise energy release retention are extrapolated from analogous dual-phase Al-containing RHEAs; no data yet exist for the exact Al–Ti–Nb–Mo–Ta–W composition, so quantitative improvements could differ by ±50 %.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce two 50 g button ingots: (A) baseline Nb25Mo25Ta25W25 and (B) modified Nb21Mo21Ta21W21Al10Ti6 (at.%). Homogenize both at 1200 °C/24 h; age alloy B at 800 °C/10 h. Machine dog-bone specimens and 6 mm-diameter, 30 mm-long impact cylinders. Perform: (1) room-temperature tensile tests (three repeats) at 10-3 s-1; (2) light-gas-gun impacts at 1 km s-1 into a steel anvil with high-speed IR thermography and post-mortem calorimetry to quantify exothermic energy.
measurements: Specific exothermic energy release (kJ g-1) during impact
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if ANY of the following are true for alloy B relative to A: (i) uniform elongation ≤5 %; (ii) 0.2 % yield strength <1.1 GPa (i.e., <85 % of baseline); or (iii) specific impact-induced energy release <0.9 H0.
